headline: Democrats win Congress: Dow jumps 3.0 percent as Brent sinks 8.8 percent and gold climbs
subhead: The S&P 500 rose 1.6 percent to 7,689 and Microsoft 6.7 percent to a record, while WTI fell 8.4 percent to 87.98 dollars, gold rose 3.7 percent and Nvidia slid 3.2 percent.

us.text: The Dow rose 3.0 percent to 53,356, its best post-midterm day since 1982, after Democrats won both chambers; the S&P 500 added 1.6 percent.
Microsoft gained 6.7, Amazon 6.1 and Apple 5.3 percent as investors bet curbs on new data centers favor incumbent cloud giants.
Micron fell 7.0, Lockheed 6.9 and Nvidia 3.2 percent on data-center and Pentagon budget worries; October payrolls are due Friday.

india.text: Nifty rose 149.75 points to 23,960.60 on Wednesday, a fifth straight gain and two-month closing high, as IT fell; price cards still show Tuesday's data.
Foreign investors net bought 7,284 crore rupees in cash on Wednesday while domestic institutions net sold 3,712 crore (provisional).
The rupee gained 17 paise to 94.58 per dollar (provisional) on easing crude, a softer dollar and foreign inflows.

global.text: Japan's Nikkei closed lower Wednesday as SoftBank, Advantest and Tokyo Electron fell on fears of tighter US rules on AI infrastructure.
Europe closed sharply higher Wednesday, the DAX near 26,438 and FTSE 100 near 10,829, on the US result; cards still show Tuesday.
Brent fell 8.8 percent to 94.51 dollars after JD Vance said the Iran war cost Republicans the midterms, fuelling de-escalation bets.

calendar.what: Bank of England decision, a hike to 4 percent widely expected; Bharti Airtel, Mahindra & Mahindra, Titan, LIC and Britannia second quarter results; MP Materials third quarter results after the US close
US October employment report; Hindalco second quarter results; Fed's Williams, Musalem and Bowman speak
India October CPI; Applied Materials and Cisco results after the US close

weekly.narrative: The week turned on whether AI spending pays: Alphabet had its worst day on record after negative free cash flow, ServiceNow and Caterpillar sank on guidance, and Intel and Amazon closed the week with a broad tech sell-off that left the Nasdaq down 2.0 percent and the S&P 500 down 0.6 percent. The Fed held rates on 28 October with two officials favouring a hike, and with oil lifted by fresh Hormuz attacks, rate fears hit metals hardest: gold lost 2.7 percent on the week to near a 52 week low and silver 8.6 percent. India moved the other way, with the Nifty back above 23,000 on IT and pharma buying, Trent jumping on results and foreign investors turning net buyers on Friday. Crypto absorbed a 6.3 billion dollar Binance hack, leaving Bitcoin down 4.8 percent in the week to 30 October. Next week brings Apple results on 2 November, the US midterm elections on 3 November, the Bank of England on 5 November and US payrolls on 6 November.
